comments.raw_text:
CCADB Policy 5.2: "An authoritative English language version of publicly available audit information MUST be uploaded to the CCADB no later than 92 calendar days from the point-in-time date or the end date of the period of time. If the audit information cannot be provided by this deadline, the CA Owner MUST instead upload an explanatory letter signed by the Qualified Auditor to Bugzilla in the 'CA Documents' component no later than 92 calendar days from the point-in-time date or the end date of the period of time."

CCADB record (2026-10-16): CA Owner "MULTICERT"; root "MULTICERT Root Certification Authority 01", SHA-256 604D32D036895AED…; Microsoft Status: Included. Standard Audit Period End Date 2026-03-31; Standard Audit Statement Date 2026-07-17 (108 days); audit URL https://pki.multicert.com/docs/aal/mtcaal2026audit.pdf. TLS BR Audit Period End Date 2023-03-31; statement 2023-06-28; nothing newer, 1,295 days ago. No letter on file: the newest CA Program bug naming MULTICERT is from 2020.

Questions: (1) Was an auditor's explanatory letter for the 2026 standard audit sent by any route? (2) Is the root still issuing TLS certificates, and if so where is the TLS BR audit for periods after 2023-03-31? (3) If it is not, should the TLS trust bit be removed from the record?

Measured at https://markovianprotocol.com/measurements/sm-012.html.

comments.author: bwilson@mozilla.com
comments.creator: bwilson@mozilla.com
comments.raw_text: The audit’s April 14 cover date predates the fieldwork, and page 9 records July 17, 2026 as the issuing date, 16 days after the July 1 deadline under CCADB Policy §5.2. MULTICERT needs to explain the date discrepancy, confirm whether a signed auditor’s letter was filed by July 1, and identify when this hierarchy last issued a publicly trusted TLS server certificate and what TLS BR audits cover the applicable periods after March 31, 2023.  FWIW, I believe that Microsoft implemented a September 15, 2025 Server Authentication cutoff.
